content: 1. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of community-acquired pneumonia caused by Chlamydophila pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, or Streptococcus pneumoniae in patients suitable for oral therapy. The recommended dosage is 500 mg orally on Day 1, followed by 250 mg orally once daily on Days 2 through 5. Alternatively, 500 mg intravenously once daily for 2 days can be followed by 500 mg orally once daily to complete a 7to 10-day course of therapy. 2. Azithromycin is indicated as an alternative therapy for the treatment of pharyngitis or tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes in individuals who cannot use first-line therapy. The recommended dosage is 500 mg orally on Day 1, followed by 250 mg orally once daily on Days 2 through 5. 3. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, or Streptococcus agalactiae. The recommended dosage is 500 mg orally on Day 1, followed by 250 mg orally once daily on Days 2 through 5. 4. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, or Streptococcus pneumoniae. The recommended dosage is 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days, or alternatively, 500 mg orally on Day 1, followed by 250 mg orally once daily on Days 2 through 5. 5. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of acute bacterial sinusitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, or Streptococcus pneumoniae. The recommended dosage is 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days. 6. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of genital ulcer disease in men caused by Haemophilus ducreyi (chancroid). The efficacy of treatment in women has not been established. The recommended dosage is 1 gram orally as a single dose. 7. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of urethritis and cervicitis caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. For non-gonococcal infections, the recommended dosage is 1 gram orally as a single dose. For gonococcal infections, the recommended dosage is 2 grams orally as a single dose. 8. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, or Mycoplasma hominis in patients requiring initial intravenous therapy. If anaerobic microorganisms are suspected, an antimicrobial agent with anaerobic activity should be administered in combination with azithromycin. The recommended dosage is 500 mg intravenously once daily for 1–2 days, followed by 250 mg orally once daily to complete a 7-day course of therapy. 9. The NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines recommend against the use of chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine and/or azithromycin for the treatment of COVID-19 in both hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients. 10. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of acute otitis media in patients aged ≥6 months caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, or Streptococcus pneumoniae. For patients <6 months, safety and efficacy have not been established. 11. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of community-acquired pneumonia in patients aged ≥6 months caused by Chlamydophila pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, or Streptococcus pneumoniae. For patients <6 months, safety and efficacy have not been established. For patients ≥6 months, the recommended dosage is 10 mg/kg orally on Day 1, followed by 5 mg/kg orally on Days 2 through 5. 12. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of acute bacterial sinusitis in patients aged ≥6 months caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, or Streptococcus pneumoniae. The recommended dosage is 10 mg/kg orally once daily for 3 days. 13. Azithromycin is indicated as an alternative therapy for the treatment of pharyngitis or tonsillitis in patients aged ≥2 years caused by Streptococcus pyogenes in individuals who cannot use first-line therapy. For patients <2 years, safety and efficacy have not been established. For patients ≥2 years, the recommended dosage is 12 mg/kg orally once daily for 5 days, not to exceed 500 mg/day. 14. Azithromycin is indicated for the treatment of non-gonococcal or gonococcal cervicitis or urethritis caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. For patients ≤45 kg, the recommended dosage is 10 mg/kg orally as a single dose, followed by 5 mg/kg orally once daily on Days 2 through 5 (not to exceed 500 mg/dose on Day 1 or 250 mg/dose on subsequent days). For patients >45 kg, the recommended dosage is 500 mg orally on Day 1, followed by 250 mg orally once daily for 4 days. 15. Azithromycin should only be used to treat infections proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria to reduce the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of azithromycin. 16. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of pimozide by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 17. Azithromycin and other drugs that prolong the QTc interval (e.g., albuterol, alfuzosin, amisulpride, anagrelide, arsenic trioxide, aripiprazole, etc.) should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, ECG monitoring is recommended to assess the risk of torsades de pointes or other serious arrhythmias. 18. Azithromycin increases the effects of antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, argatroban, and other anticoagulants by decreasing their metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Azithromycin decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., BCG vaccine, typhoid vaccine, cholera vaccine) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 20. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of drugs like colchicine, digoxin, and topotecan by altering their metabolism or efflux transport. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and adjust dosages as necessary. 21. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of drugs like cisapride, dronedarone, and ribociclib by prolonging the QTc interval. These combinations are contraindicated due to the risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias. 22. Azithromycin increases the effects of drugs like fondaparinux, heparin, and enoxaparin by decreasing their metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Azithromycin increases the levels of drugs like pomalidomide, rimegepant, and riociguat by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and exercise caution with adrenergic agonists. 25. Azithromycin increases the levels of toremifene by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid concurrent use with drugs that prolong the QT interval. If coadministration is necessary, closely monitor the patient with ECGs. 26. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of sevoflurane, siponimod, tacrolimus, and other drugs that prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Azithromycin decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 28. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ondansetron, oxaliplatin, and panobinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor ECGs if coadministration is unavoidable.
